<b>Yer istasyonu:</b> aktarma uydusunun: Ground station: the relay satellite's Earth connection is open if at least one station sees the satellite above {aci}°. Link mode: lossless = the Stage 3-4 behavior; lossy, no retransmission = a lost packet is a permanent loss (“lost on the link”); lossy + retransmission = periodic loss (every {kacinci}th attempt, average {ort}%), the sender holds the packet in its buffer for the light round-trip time (RTT) and, if it is lost, resends it up to {maks} attempts; clustered error + retransmission = the same average loss, but a two-state (good: {iyi}% / bad: {kotu}% loss, mean bad state {sure} min) clustered distribution; the state chain is produced with our own fixed-seed generator (no randomness). The link-loss slider sets the average loss in the lossy modes; the surface-link loss is fixed at {yuzey}%.
Aynı bağlantı çizelgesi altı (kavuşumsuz: The same link timeline is run with six (four on no-conjunction links) schedulers: FIFO (arrival order), priority ({siniflar}), strategy (priority + throttling science-data production before/during the conjunction; Stage 4, kept as it was) and the coverage-aware strategy (Stage 7: the same throttling, but the budget also accounts for the post-conjunction drain capacity — ground-station coverage and link-open time) and the rolling-horizon strategy (Stage 8: the same pool projection, but not tied to the conjunction flag; at every step it throttles for every closed-link period predicted from the schedule over the next “rolling horizon” — ground-station gap, behind the body, conjunction; it works at the Moon too) and the adaptive horizon (Stage 9: the same projection as rolling-horizon, but the horizon is not fixed, it is chosen according to the length of the nearby closed period in the schedule: the time remaining to the end of the period + one multiple of the period length). When a buffer overflows FIFO drops the new arrival; the others make room by discarding the newest packet of a lower class.
Kayıp, üretilmeyen ve talep: tanımlar: Loss, not produced and demand: definitions
üretilmiş ama tampon taşması yüzünden at: data that was produced but discarded because of buffer overflow.
strateji yüzünden hiç üretilmeyen (kısıl: data that was never produced (throttled) because of the strategy. Because it never entered a buffer it is not counted as dropped; it is shown in a separate column.
= üretilen + üretilmeyen: çizelgeleyicid: = produced + not produced: independent of the scheduler, the data the vehicles would have produced without throttling. The FIFO and priority schedulers do not throttle production (not produced = 0), so their demand equals what was produced.
“düşen %” = düşen / talep; “düşen + üret: “dropped %” = dropped / demand; “dropped + not produced %” = the harsher metric that does not count the strategy as having escaped loss by throttling. The strategies show both. “Delivered %” = delivered / demand.
hat hatası yüzünden maxAttempts denemede: a packet that could not be transmitted within maxAttempts attempts because of a link error (in the no-retransmission mode the first loss is permanent). It is separate from “dropped”, which is buffer overflow; it enters the loss metrics together (dropped + lost on the link [+ not produced]).
üretilen = teslim + düşen + hatta kayıp: produced = delivered + dropped + lost on the link + discarded (Stage 10 value-aware queue; 0 for the other policies) + remaining in buffers; demand = produced + not produced (verified by a test). With retransmission the sender holds the unacknowledged copy in its buffer; this counts toward buffer fill.
Teslim süresi yalnızca <i>teslim edilenl: The delivery time is computed only from delivered packets: if a scheduler drops a packet (or the strategy never produces it) its wait does not enter the average (survivorship bias). So read the time together with the loss and delivery counts. Telemetry produced during the conjunction has to wait for the end of the outage in every scheduler; so the telemetry time is close to the outage length.

Basitleştirmeler: iki atlama (araç → uyd: Simplifications: two hops (vehicle → satellite → Earth), a single link rate per hop; no coding; packets are “bulk data chunks”; when the satellite buffer is full the vehicle does not send (back-pressure) and keeps its data in its own buffer; the simulation step is {adim} s, so delivery times are coarse by at most one step. The strategies assume they know the link schedule (conjunction, ground-station coverage) in advance — the orbit and Earth's rotation are predictable; how a real mission does this is not known. The coverage-aware strategy also knows the average link loss in advance.

Paket sayıları (Teslim % hacim üzerinden: Packet counts (Delivered % is by volume, relative to demand). Demand = produced + not produced. Not produced: data the strategies throttled and never produced (not a loss). Buffered: waited in the buffer for longer than one step before delivery. Delayed: delivered after waiting in the queue for more than {dk} min. Dropped: buffer overflow. Lost on link: a packet whose attempts ran out because of link errors. Discarded (Stage 10): a science packet the value-aware queue rule discarded in the buffer because its value had fallen below the threshold (not a drop). Retransmitted: the number of packets that were lost and sent again. Produced = delivered + dropped + lost on link + discarded + remaining in buffer. Conservation check:

Link mode: {mod}. The Strategy computes the budget only from the empty buffer: with few stations (link closed most of the time) the drain after conjunction is slow and the buffer still overflows. The coverage-aware strategy adds the drain capacity to the same budget and throttles more; “dropped” falls but “not produced” rises, and the total loss (bold column) and delivered volume often change little (the link capacity is the limit). “Delivered %” relies on the same link capacity in all schedulers.

Link mode: {mod}. There is no conjunction blackout at the Moon, so the Stage 4/7 strategies do not throttle (same as priority) and are not shown; the rolling-horizon strategy foresees the station gaps and throttles: “dropped” falls, “not produced” rises, and the total loss and delivered volume mostly do not change or get slightly worse.
İkisi de aynı ortalama kayıp parametresi: Both are set up with the same average-loss parameter (Earth link {dunya}%, surface link {yuzey}%); the only difference is the distribution of the loss. Exceeding the maximum attempts ({maks}) (lost on link): {per} packets in the periodic model, {bur} packets in the clustered model. “Lost attempts %” is the realized fraction: because packets lost in the bad state are retried, attempts are over-represented in the bad state and the fraction can come out higher than the average parameter; “longest consecutive loss” shows the clustering. If the retry (RTT) is much shorter than the mean bad-state duration ({dk} min) (Moon Earth link: ~3 s; surface link: the same step) it most likely stays in the same bad state and the attempts run out; if the RTT is longer (Mars: ~40 min) the retry mostly happens after the bad state. The row without retransmission is the reference (the first loss is permanent).

Gölgeli alan: Güneş–Mars açısı {aci}° eş: Shaded area: the Sun–Mars angle is below the {aci}° threshold (blackout). During the blackout the vehicle → satellite link stays open and the satellite → Earth link is closed; the satellite buffer fills and empties when the blackout ends. Because FIFO and priority fill and empty the total occupancy almost identically the curves mostly overlap; the difference is in which data stays in the buffer and in the loss table. The strategies throttle production {gun} days before the blackout, so they fill the buffer slowly. With few ground stations (link closed most of the time) the buffer drains slowly after the blackout; the coverage-aware strategy takes this into account in advance and throttles more before the blackout, while the strategy (Stage 4) does not know and may overflow again after conjunction; the adaptive horizon chooses the horizon from the length of the closed period.
Gölgeli alanlar: Dünya hattının kapalı o: Shaded areas: the times the Earth link is closed (no ground station sees the satellite above {yuk}°, the satellite is behind the body or [Mars, if selected] in shadow; with several satellites, none of their links is open). While the link is closed the satellite buffer fills and empties when it opens; with few stations the gaps are long, the buffer fills often and may overflow. There is no conjunction: the Stage 4 and Stage 7 strategies do not throttle (identical to priority, not shown); only the rolling-horizon and adaptive strategies foresee the closed-link periods and throttle (FIFO, priority, rolling horizon and adaptive are shown).
